principle: Services, berths and throughput are physical/organizational capacities derived from design and need. Priority changes queue order, not capacity.
rules: Generate only service nodes required or justified by the facility role/design.
Berth capacity is sized from projected throughput plus explicit reserve policy; not from maximum imaginable traffic.
Larger berths capable of servicing larger ships consume disproportionate space/resources.
Repair/heavy-repair/shipyard capability require specialist teams, tools, parts and dedicated nodes.
Medical/trade/diplomatic services do not appear just because the facility is called a starbase.
Emergency priority can reorder queues but cannot create a missing berth, part, bed, specialist or capability.
Current damage, staff shortage or inventory shortage can reduce live capacity below design capacity.
Docked ship crew remains ship population unless transferred.
traffic_causality: Ships arrive because routes, missions, cargo, passengers or service needs point to the facility.
Facility does not spawn decorative traffic.
Saturation may cause holding, diversion, delayed departure or demand for expansion.
